about: Backported features from the FM-1 scene: one build switch each (firmware/src/core/backports.h; tools/build.py passes FELUCCA_x=0/1). Costs measured on feat/backports-features in the fitting config (FELUCCA_SAMPLES_SKIP=SCRCH FELUCCA_DLY_LEN=32768): the switch alone on, minus the same build with every backport switch at 0 (base 571,328 B flash, RAM 92,480 B, pool 282,192 B, RAMTEXT 32,016 B). A switch at 0 builds code and data identical to the tree without the feature (checked per feature by comparing the ELF sections). The builder shows 'notice' next to the switch; 'warning': true marks an item it must show as a WARNING (X0X-derived or experimental). X0X-derived items carry a notice in the form 'Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0). ...'.

items.title: Screen brightness: MENU > BRIGHT 1..8 (software PWM of the backlight)

source.author: Charles Vestal
source.files: firmware/hal/fm1_lcd_hw.h fm1_lcd_bl_tick, firmware/src/app/plat_fm1.c plat_brightness (8 steps of duty)

files: hooks: main.c TIMER5 ISR, ui_menu.c BRIGHT item, project.c persist_t.bright (appended)

cost.cpu: TIMER5 (10 kHz): a counter and one port write per tick

items.storage: a slot appended to the settings record (persist_t.bright), always written 0 (= full) and never applied at boot; a build without the switch reads its own record length
items.limits: It froze a real FM-1 on X0X: BRIGHTNESS 1 (duty 1/16) hung the unit, and the saved level hung it again at every boot until reflashed (X0X issue #2, 2026-10-06; X0X removed it in c6f2bf6; root cause found later: PA2 is also the /OE of the key matrix's 595s, so with the backlight line high nothing reads (Felucca 1.1.5.1, 213df5a). Here the 10 kHz tick drives PA2 low before the matrix scan, so every scan sees the 595s enabled) [R]. Here: every boot starts at full and the level is never saved (always 0 = full), and the lowest step is 4/16, not 1/16
items.notice: This backlight PWM froze an FM-1 at its lowest level on X0X (issue #2; the backlight line also enables the key matrix, which this build keeps enabled during each scan). Optimist boots at full brightness every time, never stores a dim level and never goes below 4/16, so a power-off always brings the screen back at full. Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0).

items.title: Motion recording: knob moves recorded per step (SEQ > MOTION)

source.author: Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments
source.files: firmware/src/motion.c (the 64-event store, base / active, motion_capture, motion_step), hooks in seq.c, ui_input.c, project.c

files: hooks: seq.c (motion_step, motion_begin / motion_end), project.c (capture / apply / flash), params.c MOTION page, ui_draw.c, ui_input.c (knobs, page)

cost.cpu: per step of a track with motion on: a scan of <= 64 records (sequencer, not the render)

items.storage: Since 2026-10-15 (one store, one written form): with the section log (SECTIONS 8 / 16) the automation store (motion, locks, nudges, fills, chance, conditions) is written whole in the section's and the autosave's extras record (seq/auto.h AUTO_ENC_TAG form), and a pattern record V2; the MOTN record, the SEC_MOT chunk and the 2.4 stepx form are read only (an older Optimist's projects load). Before: No project format change (FUN8 is 3,840 B = the whole sector payload). The store (200 B: the project's sum, count, on bits, 64 x 3-byte events) lives beside each project buffer in RAM (pool: 4 slots + autosave + the song's backup) and in flash in the unused bytes 32..255 of the project's own sector (between the 32-byte commit header and the payload at 256): a 208-byte record (magic, store, CRC) programmed after the project's commit; read back only when its CRC holds and its sum is the loaded project's. A build without the switch ignores it, and its next save of that slot drops it. FELUCCA_SECTIONS 8 / 16 (the sections in a log, sec_log.c): each section's record carries its motion as an optional chunk after the flags byte (sec_codec.c SEC_MOT: count, on bits, 3 bytes an event; none recorded, no chunk), power-cut safe and CRC-checked with the section, counted in the MEM gauge; the stores in RAM are the autosave's, the song backup's and those of the two buffers a section passes through (pool, bound at power-on); the first start moves each old slot's motion into its section. feat/drum-sends (FUNA: lanes in their own record at 0xE5000/0xE6000, a 4-byte key in the project) keeps the 256-byte payload offset and the 32-byte header, so the 208 B still fit (16 B spare).
items.limits: 64 events for the four tracks together (Felucca's limit); values -128..127 (every recordable parameter fits); with 4 sections, a live section stored while playing and reset before it reached flash loses its motion (8 / 16: the arena keeps it); a PRJ / AUTO backup of a 4-section build does not hold the motion; not editable from the web editor; motion edits are not undoable
items.notice: Motion recording after Felucca 1.0 by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0).

later_asm_notes.idea: tanh by its Taylor polynomial below |x| 0.5 (exact enough there), the full approximation only above: op-amp clippers and drives spend most samples in that range
later_asm_notes.for: our softclip / knee / DIST and the master knee (integer: a cubic below the knee costs two multiplies)

later_asm_notes.idea: rsqrt by two Newton steps and multiplies instead of sqrt + divide (the FPU has no sqrt; a divide is slow and traps on 0)
later_asm_notes.for: any normalisation in the FX buses; in integer form a reciprocal table + one Newton step

later_asm_notes.idea: the compressor's gain from its static curve only every 4 samples, ramped linearly between
later_asm_notes.for: our master limiter / DUCK gain: compute every 4 (or per 8) samples, ramp

later_asm_notes.idea: the limiter's divide replaced by a running reciprocal (updated when the envelope moves)
later_asm_notes.for: fx.c master_out: g = LIM_T / lim_env is a 32-bit divide per sample while limiting

later_asm_notes.idea: a filter's coefficient divide only while its cutoff moves
later_asm_notes.for: the DJ filter / tsvf_coef callers: recompute only on change

later_asm_notes.idea: silent parts not cleared, mixed or metered (exact: they would add zeros)
later_asm_notes.for: mix_block: we skip idle FX buses; parts with no voice and no tail could skip the clear and the insert chain too

compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3 (after Felucca 1.0): one stereo input, the master output (what the headphones play), MENU USB AUDIO = MASTER (follows the knob) or FULL (a second output stage at full level); MIDI and the editor on the same cable; the service runs nested in the render
compared.ours: Melodee's (FELUCCA_USB_AUDIO): 4 dry track stems in + stereo playback out, 16 / 24 bit, the X0X cubic resampler to the host's clock (always built since 2026-10-15), MIDI and the editor on the same cable
compared.evidence: fm1-emulator tests/usb_audio_firmware.rs on the real user-default build (2026-10-06): 16 and 24 bit, 2,450 capture / playback packets, missed 0, lost 0, feedback 44.10 frames/ms, the four stems bit-exact against the mixer taps, host playback against the DAC, USB-MIDI notes and the editor's INFO reply over USB-MIDI while streaming, no late half. Theirs has no stems and no playback; its one gain, recording the master mix with the effects, is not ported (a 6-channel capture: new descriptors, +4 KiB pool, 810 B a frame at 24 bit; not tried on hardware)

compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3 (after Felucca 1.0): pulses taken in the render's block loop at fm1_ms (1 ms) resolution, the position interpolated from the last interval, the USB poll held off during a render; SYNC a setting of the FM-1
compared.ours: clock_sync.c: every byte / packet timestamped at the 10 kHz tick, latency-compensated, steps at the sample; SYNC AUTO / INT / USB / TRS, kept in the project
compared.evidence: tests/clock_sync_test.c (ours, make test): phase vs the ideal F8, USB 120 BPM +-1 ms jitter: mean +0.04, p95 0.15, max 0.22 ms; steady 0.01 ms. A model of 2.3's mclk_event / mclk_adv with the firmware's timing (a one-off script, 256-sample halves, 2 kHz poll not during a render): ~10.3-11.0 ms late on average (no latency compensation) and a spread about that of p95 1.8-2.7 ms, max 2.5-3.5 ms, at render loads of 30 % and 60 %

compared.what: TRS MIDI IN buffer read by content
compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3 (Felucca [Salt] 0.9-salt14, ChanceTheMaker): the 2 kHz poll drains the ring by content, an FD at the reader passed over once the next byte lands
compared.ours: Melodee's read by content (the same fix), at the 10 kHz peek with byte times for the clock
compared.verdict: kept ours, took their FD handling (FELUCCA_TRS_NOISE)
compared.evidence: tests/midi_uart_test.c: with an FD landed at the reader, our peek never drained (the jack deaf until a restart); with the switch the note after it is read

compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3: protocol v6 (BK_LIST / GET / PUT, 34..36): working project, settings, 4 projects, 2 preset banks, 3 sample slots; each object checked at commit as a load checks it
compared.ours: ed_backup.c (43..48): every stored object incl. the drum records, the kit bank, the FM6 bank, the section log and the song chain, older backups migrated, one session flushed first, a restart when done
compared.verdict: kept ours, took their per-object check (FELUCCA_BK_CHECK)
compared.evidence: tests/backup_test.c: a FUNA project with a wrong sum, a non-project, a kit bank or drum record of the wrong shape refused at COMMIT (rc 8) and the old object kept; every object still round-trips

compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3 (after Felucca 1.0): the exact official FM-1.fwsc (SHA-256), a backup checkbox, a resumed return checked once the FM-1 is back (FM-1_015)
compared.ours: after Felucca 1.0.1: the same SHA-256 pin, a resumed return only with the official loader (OFFICIAL_LOADER)
compared.verdict: kept ours, took the identity check after a resumed return (web/fm1ota.js resume(..., product))
compared.evidence: web/test_web.mjs: a resumed return reports done only when the FM-1 comes back as FM-1_015; another identity is 'mismatch'

compared.theirs: SLOOP 2.3 = Felucca 1.0's (#23): one rest state, whole cycles, a two-scan filter
compared.ours: Felucca 1.6's decoder (hugelton/Felucca, unchanged since 1.1.5 276f72a #126): one rest state, no two-scan filter (X0X b637df3 first), a two-state jump from the detent the way of a click of the last 20 frames; plus acceleration (KNOB_ACCEL)
compared.verdict: taken whole, always built (2026-10-14): FELUCCA_KNOB_ONEREST retired, the 0.9 learner and Melodee's first-click fix gone with it
compared.evidence: tests/encoder_felucca_test.c (Felucca 1.6 #63 / #126 cases): our 0.9 learner path failed 80 of 720 fast turns and 20 slow bouncy ones; the merged ONEREST decoder and Felucca's pass all; encoder_onerest_test.c (SLOOP 2.3), encoder_fast_test.c (X0X) pass
